title: HttpClientFactory
description: HttpClientFactory is a factory for creating HttpClient instances in ASP.NET Core. It manages DNS changes, socket exhaustion, and integrates with Polly for resilience.

data.text: HttpClientFactory manages the lifetime of HttpClient instances. It prevents socket exhaustion by pooling handlers, handles DNS refresh automatically, and integrates seamlessly with Polly policies.

terms.definition: A class that receives an HttpClient via constructor injection, encapsulating API logic.
The service that creates and manages HttpClient instances with pooling.
HttpClientFactory reuses HttpMessageHandler instances to avoid socket exhaustion.

data.title: Avoid new HttpClient()
data.text: Creating a new HttpClient for every request can exhaust sockets. Use IHttpClientFactory or reuse a single HttpClient instance instead.

Creating a new `HttpClient` per request looks harmless but exhausts sockets because each disposed client closes a connection. A single static client avoids that but pins DNS forever. `IHttpClientFactory` solves both: it pools the underlying handlers, rotates them on a schedule to pick up DNS changes, and hands out cheap clients that can be created per request.

data.title: A typed client with a testable handler stack
Where a DelegatingHandler earns its place
data.text: A `DelegatingHandler` sits in the request pipeline and is the right home for cross-cutting HTTP concerns: adding an auth header, logging correlation ids, or applying a Polly pipeline. Because it is registered with the client rather than written in the calling code, every call through the typed client gets the behavior for free.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Typed clients encapsulate API logic in dedicated classes
data.takeaway: HttpClientFactory is the recommended way to use HttpClient in modern .NET.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Typed Client
data.description: Create a typed client for a weather API.
steps: Create an IWeatherService interface with a GetForecastAsync method
Implement WeatherService that accepts HttpClient in its constructor
Register the typed client with AddHttpClient<IWeatherService, WeatherService>()
Inject IWeatherService into a controller or minimal API endpoint
Call the endpoint and display the forecast data
data.expectedOutcome: A working typed client that fetches weather data through HttpClientFactory.
